title: How tall are the date palm trees on this farm?
description: The heights of twenty nine date palm trees are put on a dot plot. The video finds the median, finds the mean by a quicker route from a guess, and counts the trees shorter than the mean.
teaching_notes: One idea: a good guess makes the mean quick, because only the small differences from the guess need adding. Watch for students who forget that the differences below the guess count as negative.

source: Heights of date palm trees on a farm: dot plot, mean, median, a quicker mean, trees shorter than the mean
video_script.why: The child has found the median by sorting and the mean by sharing, and now looks for a quicker way to the mean.
video_script.substitution: Sort for the middle tree, then guess a height and add only the differences from the guess.
video_script.payoff_line: The mean is about fifty five point nine feet and the median is fifty six feet.

final_answer.value: mean 55.9 feet, median 56 feet, 13 trees shorter than the mean
final_answer.spoken: mean fifty five point nine feet, median fifty six feet, thirteen trees shorter

maths_rules: guess 55: trees above 55 add 91 feet, trees below 55 take away 65 feet; 91 - 65 = 26
the mean is between 55 and 56, so the trees of 55 feet or less are shorter: 13 trees; 16 trees are 56 feet or more; 13 + 16 = 29
video_script.design: One idea: guess, then add the differences. The dot plot builds on the stage; a guess line at fifty five lets the dots above it and below it be counted as differences.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book about a farm of date palm trees.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The farmer measured the heights of twenty nine trees, in feet.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The board shows every height.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>We want the mean and the median height.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Will the mean and the median be close together, or far apart?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, sort the heights and find the middle tree.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>There are twenty nine trees, so the middle one is the fifteenth.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Its height is fifty six feet, so the median is fifty six feet.

beats.on_screen: guess 55 feet; above the guess: +91 feet; below the guess: −65 feet; 91 − 65 = 26

marks.m1: a guess line appears at 55 feet
marks.m2: the dots above the line show +91 feet in all
marks.m3: the dots below the line show −65 feet in all

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, guess a height near the middle, say fifty five feet.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The trees above the guess are taller by ninety one feet in all.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The trees below the guess are shorter by sixty five feet in all.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Ninety one take away sixty five leaves twenty six extra feet.

marks.m1: the 26 extra feet are shared among 29 boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, share the twenty six extra feet equally among the twenty nine trees.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The mean is the guess plus twenty six shared by twenty nine.

beats.on_screen: Check: 26 ÷ 29 is under 1, so the mean is between 55 and 56; 13 trees are 55 or less; 16 trees are 56 or more; 13 + 16 = 29

marks.m1: the mean marker sits between 55 and 56
marks.m2: the 13 dots at 55 or less glow

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check where the mean sits and count.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twenty six shared by twenty nine is less than one. The mean sits between fifty five and fifty six.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Thirteen trees are fifty five feet or less, and sixteen trees are fifty six feet or more.
